A speed-reading method that times each paragraph with a stopwatch
A way of ranking daily tasks by deadline and doing the earliest first

questions.q: Why is each interval called a pomodoro?
options: Named for the Italian town where Cirillo was born
After a university course on Italian cooking Cirillo took
After the tomato-shaped kitchen timer Cirillo used
After the red pencil Cirillo used to mark finished tasks
questions.explain: Pomodoro is Italian for tomato, after Cirillo's kitchen timer.

questions.q: How long is the long break after four pomodori?
options: 5 to 10 minutes
15 minutes
Exactly one hour
20 to 30 minutes
questions.explain: A long break is typically 20 to 30 minutes.

questions.q: In the study of 25 students versus 35 taking self-regulated breaks, what did the self-regulated group do?
options: Chose shorter sessions, linked to lower fatigue
Chose longer study sessions, linked to higher fatigue
Reported higher motivation and better concentration
Completed more tasks than the Pomodoro group
questions.explain: They chose longer sessions linked to higher fatigue and lower concentration and motivation.

questions.q: Why do proponents prefer a mechanical timer, paper and pencil?
options: Physical stimuli like winding and ticking become tied to flow and focus
Digital apps are too expensive for most students to afford
Paper lists are faster to read than apps, which saves minutes
Software cannot count pomodori accurately across several devices
questions.explain: Winding confirms determination, ticking externalizes the desire, and ringing announces a break.
